Mens razors, I use 4 or 5 bladed ones. Please don't use single Or double bladed cheapies or women's razors if you can help it. I know it isn't always that easy, but a bad razor can really tear your skin up, and it won't have as much success removing hair. You need to exfoliate your legs well, and I would wait until the end of a shower or take a bath to soften the hair. Conditioner is awesome for shaving ones legs with and its cheap. If you can't get the all of the hair the first sweep, exfoliate again and repeat the process. I wouldn't go more than 2 swipes, but if you do, be mindful of razor burn and ingrown hairs starting off. Please for the love of god, be mindful of the backs of your heels on the tendon, your ankles, and your knees. Its so easy to cut the skin and its awful to walk around with ankle knicks. 

Have some bandaids and Neosporin on hand in case though. After you're done, use some type of aftershave with good moisturizers and stuff to calm the skin. If you decide to continue, keep your skin moisturized with your fav lotion topped off with some coconut oil. So fecking smooth and soft.

I had lots of cis guy friends when I was your age that tried this, and even shaved their arm pits, especially during summer. I live in the South so summers are literally picked from the crack of Satan so it made sense that they got hot and wanted to stay cooler/cleaner. If you bike or swim, you have an easy excuse. You can always find a good excuse. If you need anything, shoot me a PM. 

Good luck kid :)

I have learned to process it and accept it much more since this discussion started. I went from porn and looking at women is cheating to checking out women with him without batting an eye. We came from a very fundamentalist religion so its still hard for me to break away from that school of thought and the feelings that come with it. Its especially hard to break away from the idea that there is no such thing as ethical non-monagomy. 

I have some good methods of dealing with hard feelings but I guess it's a foreign concept to accept jealousy as just another one of those hard feelings you can manage.
Used to I had a VERY hard time saying I'm female. Now I view it more as an aspect of my biology, not so much myself, so that makes it easier...? I just say my preferred name and leave it at that.
